question: For overweight or obese adults, what did a meta-analysis of randomized trials find when time-restricted eating was added to caloric restriction, compared with caloric restriction alone?
options: It produced greater losses of body weight, fat mass, and waist circumference, but no additional improvement in blood lipids or glucose.
It produced no greater loss of body weight, fat mass, or waist circumference than caloric restriction alone.
It produced greater improvements in LDL cholesterol, triglycerides, and fasting glucose than caloric restriction alone.
The extra weight loss occurred only when food intake was confined to the late part of the day.
gold_answer: It produced greater losses of body weight, fat mass, and waist circumference, but no additional improvement in blood lipids or glucose.
notes: Calibration item. Every passage was checked against PMC10708501 on 2026-11-19. Human verification, independent annotation, and adjudication are still required. Option D is an unused distractor; agents 0 and 2 argue different wrong positions so the item tests evidence-weighted trust rather than simple vote counting.

positions.answer: It produced no greater loss of body weight, fat mass, or waist circumference than caloric restriction alone.

claims.text: Adding time-restricted eating to caloric restriction did not produce significantly greater body-weight loss.

evidence.text: The MD of BW change between groups using a fixed-effect model was −2.11 kg (95% CI: −2.68 kg to −1.54 kg, p = < 0.00001, I2 = 42%) (Figure 3), indicating a significantly greater BW loss in the TRE with CR group compared with the CR group.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports a significantly greater body-weight loss with TRE plus CR than with CR alone (MD −2.11 kg, 95% CI −2.68 to −1.54 kg, p < 0.00001).

claims.text: Fat-mass loss did not differ significantly between the two groups.

evidence.text: Overall, the TRE with CR group exhibited a significantly greater reduction in FM than the control group with CR (MD: −0.75 kg, 95% CI: −1.35 kg to −0.16 kg, p = 0.01; I2 = 0%) (Figure 5a).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states a significantly greater reduction in fat mass with TRE plus CR than with CR alone (MD −0.75 kg, 95% CI −1.35 to −0.16 kg, p = 0.01).

claims.text: Waist circumference changed by the same amount in both groups.

evidence.text: The results showed a statistically significantly greater reduction of WC in the TRE group with CR compared with the control group with CR (MD: −1.27 cm, 95% CI: −2.36 cm to −0.19 cm, p = 0.02, I2 = 0%) (Figure 6).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports a statistically significantly greater reduction in waist circumference with TRE plus CR (MD −1.27 cm, 95% CI −2.36 to −0.19 cm, p = 0.02).

positions.answer: It produced greater losses of body weight, fat mass, and waist circumference, but no additional improvement in blood lipids or glucose.

claims.text: Body-weight loss was significantly greater with time-restricted eating plus caloric restriction (mean difference −2.11 kg).

evidence.text: The MD of BW change between groups using a fixed-effect model was −2.11 kg (95% CI: −2.68 kg to −1.54 kg, p = < 0.00001, I2 = 42%) (Figure 3), indicating a significantly greater BW loss in the TRE with CR group compared with the CR group.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage directly reports a significantly greater BW loss with TRE plus CR, with a mean difference of −2.11 kg (95% CI −2.68 to −1.54 kg).

claims.text: There was no significant between-group difference in fasting glucose, LDL cholesterol, or triglycerides.

evidence.text: There were no significant differences in FG changes after the interventions between all TRE groups with CR and control groups with CR (MD: 0.14 mg/dL, 95% CI: −0.87 mg/dL to 1.15 mg/dL, p = 0.79, I2 = 35%) (Figure 8a).

Indeed, the fixed-effect model showed no significant difference in TC changes (MD: 0.98 mg/dL, 95% CI: −2.19 mg/dL to 4.15 mg/dL, p = 0.54, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8b), changes in HDL (MD: 1.71 mg/dL, 95% CI: −0.22 mg/dL to 3.65 mg/dL, p = 0.08, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8c), changes in LDL (MD: −0.77 mg/dL, 95% CI: −2.59 mg/dL to 1.05 mg/dL, p = 0.41, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8d), and changes in TG levels (MD: 2.26 mg/dL, 95% CI: −4.43 mg/dL to 8.96 mg/dL, p = 0.51, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8e) between all TRE groups with CR and the control groups with CR.

claims.verdict_rationale: The first passage reports no significant difference in fasting glucose (p = 0.79); the second reports no significant differences in LDL (p = 0.41) and triglycerides (p = 0.51) between TRE with CR and CR alone.

claims.text: The additional weight loss was not accompanied by a significant loss of fat-free mass.

evidence.text: There was no significant difference in FFM changes in the TRE with CR group vs. the control group with CR (MD: −0.22 kg, 95% CI: −0.68 kg to 0.25 kg, p = 0.36, I2 = 0%) (Figure 5b).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states there was no significant difference in fat-free-mass changes between TRE with CR and CR alone (MD −0.22 kg, 95% CI −0.68 to 0.25 kg, p = 0.36).

positions.answer: It produced greater improvements in LDL cholesterol, triglycerides, and fasting glucose than caloric restriction alone.

claims.text: LDL cholesterol fell significantly more with time-restricted eating added to caloric restriction.

evidence.text: Indeed, the fixed-effect model showed no significant difference in TC changes (MD: 0.98 mg/dL, 95% CI: −2.19 mg/dL to 4.15 mg/dL, p = 0.54, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8b), changes in HDL (MD: 1.71 mg/dL, 95% CI: −0.22 mg/dL to 3.65 mg/dL, p = 0.08, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8c), changes in LDL (MD: −0.77 mg/dL, 95% CI: −2.59 mg/dL to 1.05 mg/dL, p = 0.41, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8d), and changes in TG levels (MD: 2.26 mg/dL, 95% CI: −4.43 mg/dL to 8.96 mg/dL, p = 0.51, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8e) between all TRE groups with CR and the control groups with CR.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states there was no significant difference in LDL changes between TRE with CR and CR alone (MD −0.77 mg/dL, 95% CI −2.59 to 1.05 mg/dL, p = 0.41), contradicting a significantly greater fall.

claims.text: Triglycerides fell significantly more in the time-restricted-eating group.

evidence.text: Indeed, the fixed-effect model showed no significant difference in TC changes (MD: 0.98 mg/dL, 95% CI: −2.19 mg/dL to 4.15 mg/dL, p = 0.54, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8b), changes in HDL (MD: 1.71 mg/dL, 95% CI: −0.22 mg/dL to 3.65 mg/dL, p = 0.08, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8c), changes in LDL (MD: −0.77 mg/dL, 95% CI: −2.59 mg/dL to 1.05 mg/dL, p = 0.41, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8d), and changes in TG levels (MD: 2.26 mg/dL, 95% CI: −4.43 mg/dL to 8.96 mg/dL, p = 0.51, I2 = 0%) (Figure 8e) between all TRE groups with CR and the control groups with CR.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states there was no significant difference in triglyceride changes (MD 2.26 mg/dL, 95% CI −4.43 to 8.96 mg/dL, p = 0.51) and the point estimate is positive, not a greater fall.

claims.text: The greater weight loss occurred only in trials with more than 100 participants per group.

evidence.text: Our meta-analysis included seven studies with nine interventions and 458 participants.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports only the total number of studies, interventions, and participants; it contains no sample-size-stratified weight-loss estimates, so it neither establishes nor refutes the claimed threshold.
